plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 11: Angular Momentum
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional diagram of a spinning top together with the vectors that govern its precession. A coordinate frame is drawn with z vertical, y to the right, and x angled toward the lower left, meeting at the origin O where the point of the top rests. The top is a rounded, banded body in blue and orange capped by a short cylindrical stem, its symmetry axis tilted away from z by the angle theta. A heavy black arrow labeled r runs from O to the center of mass, marked with an X and labeled 'CM', where a red arrow labeled 'M g' points straight down. From that same point an orange arrow labeled tau extends outward and slightly upward, with a curved leader to the expression 'tau = r x M g'. A green loop labeled omega circles the stem to give the spin sense, and a long orange arrow labeled L lies along the tilted axis, reaching a dashed horizontal circle drawn above the top. On that circle a radial orange arrow labeled 'L sin theta' and a tangential arrow labeled 'dL = tau dt' meet at a small angle marked 'd phi', while a curved black arrow labeled omega sub p at the upper left gives the direction of precession. Placing the torque perpendicular to L lets the reader see that the tip of L sweeps around the circle instead of tipping over. The construction sets up the calculation of how fast a gravitationally torqued top precesses about the vertical.

elements: 3D coordinate frame with origin O at the pointed pivot of the top
vertical z-axis rising from O with arrowhead and label z at the top
horizontal y-axis extending to the right from O with arrowhead and label y
x-axis extending diagonally down-left from O with arrowhead and label x
rounded spinning-top body, pointed at O and bulging near the upper half
translucent blue upper and lower regions of the top body
wide orange band wrapping around the middle of the top body
elliptical top rim of the body
short cylindrical stem emerging from the top face along the tilted symmetry axis
top ellipse of the stem
tilted symmetry axis of the top running from O through CM and the stem
black position vector r from O to the center of mass along the tilted body axis
angle arc θ between the vertical z-axis and r near the lower part of the top
center of mass marker drawn as a black X on the tilted axis and labeled CM
red downward force vector labeled Mg starting at CM
orange torque vector τ starting at CM, perpendicular to the r-Mg plane
curved black leader from the torque vector to the label τ = r × Mg on the right
green circular spin arrow around the stem labeled ω
long orange angular momentum vector L along the tilted symmetry axis, pointing upward to the precession circle
horizontal dashed precession circle centered on the z-axis above the top
black curved arrow on the dashed precession circle labeled ωp showing the precession direction
dashed radial construction line from the z-axis to the tip of L
orange radial construction arrow labeled L sinθ from the z-axis to the L tip
small angular arc at the center of the dashed circle labeled dφ
orange tangential increment arrow labeled dL = τdt attached to the tip of L
all vector labels: r, θ, CM, Mg, τ, τ = r × Mg, ω, L, L sinθ, dφ, dL = τdt, ωp, O, x, y, z

interactions.label: Play precession
interactions.teaches: The angular momentum vector keeps a constant length while its tip moves around a horizontal circle, so torque changes the direction of L rather than increasing its magnitude

interactions.label: Tilt angle θ
interactions.teaches: Changing the lean changes the radius L sinθ of the circular path traced by the tip of L, which changes the geometric size of each precession angle dφ

interactions.label: Torque magnitude |τ|
interactions.teaches: A larger torque makes the tangential change dL longer while the L arrow itself stays the same length, emphasizing that torque redirects angular momentum

demo_steps.title: Default precessing top
demo_steps.narration: The top leans by about 25°. The orange L vector lies along the tilted axis and its tip sits on the dashed precession circle.

demo_steps.title: Increase the tilt
demo_steps.narration: As θ grows, the dashed circle and the L sinθ construction become wider. The same length L now sweeps a larger radius around the vertical axis.

demo_steps.title: Increase the torque
demo_steps.narration: With θ fixed, increasing |τ| lengthens the tangential dL = τdt arrow. The L vector remains the same length, showing that the torque turns L rather than stretching it.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a 3D axonometric diagram matching the source orientation: z is vertical on screen, y points screen-right, and x points diagonally down-left. World scale: pivot O at (0,0,0); z-axis length about 5.2 units; y-axis length about 3.5 units; x-axis length about 2.2 units. Let the top symmetry axis lie in the visual z-y plane at default θ = 25°, leaning to the viewer’s upper right. Top body height from O to upper rim about 2.9 units; maximum body radius about 1.15 units near z ≈ 1.8 along the tilted local axis; pointed lower end at O; rounded shoulder at the top. Create the body as a lathe or custom surface around the tilted local axis with radius profile approximately: radius 0 at local height 0, 0.65 at 0.8, 1.15 at 1.65, 1.05 at 2.35, 0.75 at 2.75. The middle orange band wraps around local heights 0.95 to 1.65; blue translucent regions above and below. Dominant colors: translucent blue body #62b7cf with opacity about 0.65, orange band #ffd37a, darker blue outlines #238ca8, green spin arrow #7fa82a, orange vectors #f28c00, red weight vector #c8324a, black axes and r vector #111111. Stem: short cylinder coaxial with the top, radius about 0.22 units, length about 1.0 unit, starting at the top rim and leaning with the same θ; color blue #62b7cf with darker rim. CM is on the tilted axis about 1.85 units above O along the local axis. r runs from O to CM in black with arrowhead at CM. Mg starts at CM and points vertically downward about 1.25 units. τ starts at CM and points tangentially around the z-axis, roughly screen-right/up in the source view, length controlled by torqueMagnitude; keep it perpendicular to the plane containing r and Mg. L is fixed length about 3.3 units, collinear with the tilted axis, extending upward from near the top/stem to its tip on the precession circle. The dashed precession circle is horizontal, centered on the z-axis at the height of the L tip; its radius is L sinθ. At default θ=25° and L=3.3, radius ≈ 1.39 units. The vertical height of the L tip above O is L cosθ plus the chosen base offset, visually around z ≈ 4.1. The radial construction arrow L sinθ lies in the circle plane from the z-axis to the L tip. dL = τdt is tangent to the dashed circle at the L tip, with length proportional to torqueMagnitude; use dφ ≈ |dL|/(L sinθ) for the small angle arc. Precession animation rotates the tilted top body, r, CM, τ, L, L sinθ, dL, and the construction point around the z-axis while preserving θ and |L|. The dashed circle remains horizontal and centered on z.
interactionPlan.notes: Use transparent materials with depth sorting handled carefully so the internal r and Mg arrows remain readable over the body. Render vector arrows with cylinders plus cones or ArrowHelper-style geometry, but keep arrowheads large enough to match the textbook style. Use dashed line material for the precession circle and radial construction guide. Text labels should be billboarded toward the camera and placed close to the corresponding source positions: z at the top axis, y at the right arrowhead, x at lower-left arrowhead, O at the pivot, CM beside the X, τ = r × Mg to the right with a curved leader. During animation, keep the camera fixed and rotate the physical/construction group about the vertical z-axis; the spin arrow around the stem may also rotate faster locally to suggest rapid spin, but the central teaching focus is the slow precession of L.

authoredContext:
The figure shows the forces acting on a spinning top. The torque produced is perpendicular to the angular momentum vector. This changes the direction of the angular momentum vector L→ according to dL→=τ→dt, but not its magnitude. The top precesses around a vertical axis, since the torque is always horizontal and perpendicular to L→. If the top is not spinning, it acquires angular momentum in the direction of the torque, and it rotates around a horizontal axis, falling over just as we would expect.

We can calculate the precession rate of the top in the figure. From the figure, we see that the magnitude of the torque is

The force of gravity acting on the center of mass produces a torque τ→ in the direction perpendicular to L→. The magnitude of L→ doesn’t change but its direction does, and the top precesses about the z-axis.

An x y z coordinate system is show, with x out of the page, y to the right, and z up. The origin is point O. A top is shown with its point at the origin and its axis tilted by an angle theta away from the vertical z axis, clockwise as we view it. The vector r extends from the origin to the center of the mass, labeled as C M, of the top. The force M g acts downward at the center of mass. The torque, tau, about the origin is equal to vector r crossed with M vector g. This torque is a vector in the x y plane, perpendicular to the r vector, into the page. The angular velocity, omega, of the top is counterclockwise as viewed from above. The angular momentum, L, is in the same direction as the r vector, tilted up along the axis of the top. The circle traced by the precession of the top is shown as a horizontal circle above the top. The precession angular velocity omega sub p is counterclockwise as viewed from above. The radius of the precession circle is L sine theta. The vector d L is tangent to the circle, pointing into the page, and is equal to vector tau d t. The triangle formed L sine theta and d L is shown, and the angle across from d L is labeled as d phi.

We can experience this phenomenon first hand by holding a spinning bicycle wheel and trying to rotate it about an axis perpendicular to the spin axis. As shown in the figure, the person applies forces perpendicular to the spin axis in an attempt to rotate the wheel, but instead, the wheel axis starts to change direction to her left due to the applied torque.

interactions.label: Play precession
interactions.teaches: The angular momentum vector keeps a constant length while its tip moves around a horizontal circle, so torque changes the direction of L rather than increasing its magnitude

interactions.label: Tilt angle θ
interactions.teaches: Changing the lean changes the radius L sinθ of the circular path traced by the tip of L, which changes the geometric size of each precession angle dφ

interactions.label: Torque magnitude |τ|
interactions.teaches: A larger torque makes the tangential change dL longer while the L arrow itself stays the same length, emphasizing that torque redirects angular momentum

demo_steps.title: Default precessing top
demo_steps.narration: The top leans by about 25°. The orange L vector lies along the tilted axis and its tip sits on the dashed precession circle.

demo_steps.title: Increase the tilt
demo_steps.narration: As θ grows, the dashed circle and the L sinθ construction become wider. The same length L now sweeps a larger radius around the vertical axis.

demo_steps.title: Increase the torque
demo_steps.narration: With θ fixed, increasing |τ| lengthens the tangential dL = τdt arrow. The L vector remains the same length, showing that the torque turns L rather than stretching it.
